# Custom AsciiDoc components

Source: /prerelease/main/reference-custom-asciidoc-components/

This site’s own blocks, registered by `@inditextech/docouture-asciidoc-extensions` and documented in full in the `docouture-writing-docs-pages` skill’s `reference/docouture-blocks.md`. Every one of these degrades to plain, readable HTML with JavaScript disabled. See [AsciiDoc basics](../reference-asciidoc-basics/) for plain AsciiDoc first, and [Integrations](../reference-integrations/) for the build-time capabilities (diagrams, syntax highlighting) mentioned below, in full. Same pattern throughout: raw markup first, then the same markup rendered live.

## Tabs

A switcher for equivalent alternatives. Each `[tabs]` block is independent — picking a tab in one never affects another further down the page.

```
[tabs]
--
[tab,label="pnpm"]
****
[,bash]
----
pnpm add some-package
----
****

[tab,label="npm"]
****
[,bash]
----
npm install some-package
----
****

[tab,label="yarn"]
****
[,bash]
----
yarn add some-package
----
****
--
```

- pnpm
- npm
- yarn

```
pnpm add some-package
```

```
npm install some-package
```

```
yarn add some-package
```

A second, independent set:

```
[tabs]
--
[tab,label="pnpm"]
****
[,bash]
----
pnpm run dev
----
****

[tab,label="npm"]
****
[,bash]
----
npm run dev
----
****
--
```

- pnpm
- npm

```
pnpm run dev
```

```
npm run dev
```

## Cards

Text-only — no image, no open block needed:

```
[cards]
====
[card]
.xref:main:quickstart.adoc[Quickstart]
Scaffold, build, publish — the smallest path to a working result.

[card,subheader="Reference"]
.xref:main:guides-adding-a-page.adoc[Adding a page]
Create a file, add it to nav.adoc, done.

[card,icon="design/grid-outlined"]
.xref:main:architecture.adoc[Architecture]
This one carries a header icon — `icon=` and `subheader=` share one header row and
combine fine on the same card, they aren't alternatives to each other.
====
```

[Quickstart](../quickstart/)

Scaffold, build, publish — the smallest path to a working result.

Reference

[Adding a page](../guides-adding-a-page/)

Create a file, add it to nav.adoc, done.

[Architecture](../architecture/)

This one carries a header icon — `icon=` and `subheader=` share one header row and combine fine on the same card, they aren’t alternatives to each other.

`icon=` takes a `group/name` string, and only renders if that icon has a generated CSS mask — see [Icon gallery](../guides-icon-gallery/) for the full, working set. A per-card `labels=` attribute (comma-separated) renders a separate row of small grey chips, independent of `subheader=`.

With images, a fixed square aspect, four columns, let out to the container’s full width — the same shape the landing’s own quicklinks use (`ROOT:card-placeholder.png` reused across modules via a cross-module image resource ID):

```
[cards,type=image-square,columns="1 s:2 m:4",width=container]
====
[card,subheader="One"]
.xref:main:quickstart.adoc[First]
--
image::ROOT:card-placeholder.png[Placeholder card image]

Every card in a block shares one aspect ratio.
--

[card,subheader="Two"]
.xref:main:index.adoc[Second]
--
image::ROOT:card-placeholder.png[Placeholder card image]

The image crops to fill; it is never letterboxed.
--
====
```

![Placeholder card image](../../_images/card-placeholder.png)

One

[First](../quickstart/)

Every card in a block shares one aspect ratio.

![Placeholder card image](../../_images/card-placeholder.png)

Two

[Second](../)

The image crops to fill; it is never letterboxed.

- `type=` — `no-image` (default), `image-landscape`, `image-square`, or `image-portrait`.
- `columns=` — space-separated `breakpoint:count` tokens (a bare number sets the base/mobile count); breakpoints are `s`, `m`, `l` only, up to 4 columns each. Defaults to `"1 s:2 m:3"` if omitted.
- `width=` — `content` (default, matches the page’s text measure) or `container` (full page width, as above).

## Accordion

Groups a run of `[%collapsible]` items with `role=group` semantics. `%single-open` closes whichever other item was open; without it, items are independent.

```
[accordion%single-open,aria-label="Single-open example"]
--
.First question?
[%collapsible]
====
First answer.
====

.Second question?
[%collapsible]
====
Second answer. Opening this closes the first.
====
--
```

First question?

First answer.

Second question?

Second answer. Opening this closes the first.

Grouped, but independent (the default — no `%single-open`):

```
[accordion,aria-label="Multiple-open example"]
--
.Can both of these be open at once?
[%collapsible]
====
Yes — this group has no `%single-open`, so each item toggles independently.
====

.Is this still one accessible group?
[%collapsible]
====
Yes — `aria-label=` (or a block `.Title`) names the group as a whole.
====
--
```

Can both of these be open at once?

Yes — this group has no `%single-open`, so each item toggles independently.

Is this still one accessible group?

Yes — `aria-label=` (or a block `.Title`) names the group as a whole.

## Diagrams

`[mermaid]`, `[plantuml]`, `[graphviz]` and a handful of other diagram languages (see `@inditextech/docouture-asciidoc-extensions’ `lib/kroki-config.js` for the full list) render as real diagrams via a self-hosted [Kroki](https://kroki.io) service — a literal block (four dots, not a fenced code block) styled with the diagram language’s name:

```
[mermaid]
....
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Running : start
  Running --> Idle : stop
....
```

This feature is **enabled by default** in this starter (see `antora-playbook.yml’s `kroki-enabled`/`kroki-diagram-types` attributes) — it needs [Docker](https://www.docker.com) available, since the build starts a self-hosted Kroki service the first time a build needs it, no manual step required (it isn’t stopped automatically either — run `docouture teardown kroki` once you’re done with it). Run `docouture eject kroki` if you ever need to customize the container definition, or comment the two attributes back out to turn the feature off entirely — a block like the one above then renders exactly as plain AsciiDoc already would: the raw diagram source, as literal text, same as the fenced listing shows it above.

### Styling

[Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) diagrams are themed to match the IOP Design System automatically — square corners, black-on-white (light mode; inverted for dark), body typography — via a `%%{init: {…​}}%%` directive this extension prepends to the diagram’s own source before it ever reaches Kroki, not via CSS. Write your own `%%{init…​}%%` as the diagram’s first line to opt out and take full control of Mermaid’s own theming instead. Every other diagram type’s font is still normalized via CSS (safe — a tool’s typeface choice carries no meaning); [BPMN](https://www.bpmn.org)'s two-tone palette is still remapped via CSS too (its [bpmn-js](https://bpmn.io) renderer has no source-level theming hook this package uses yet, unlike Mermaid’s). BPMN’s own rounded task-box corners could not be un-rounded by any means found — bpmn-js hardcodes that radius; this is a real, currently-unfixed limitation, not an oversight.

### PNG output

`[mermaid,format=png]` (or any other diagram language Kroki can rasterize — see `kroki-config.js’s `PNG_SUPPORTED_TYPES` for the full list; `bpmn` and `excalidraw` are notably **not** on it, Kroki itself rejects `/bpmn/png` and `/excalidraw/png` outright) renders a transparent PNG instead of inline SVG:

```
[mermaid,format=png]
....
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Running : start
  Running --> Idle : stop
....
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Embedded as a plain `<img>` with a base64 `data:` URI — no extra file written, no extra HTTP request. Reach for this only when you actually need a raster image (an export, an email, a renderer that can’t handle inline SVG); the inline-SVG default stays sharper at every zoom level and lets a reader select/search the diagram’s own text, neither of which a PNG can do. An unsupported type or a typo’d `format=` value both fall back to `svg` with a build warning, the same degrade-not-fail posture as an unknown `kroki-diagram-types` entry.

### BPMN

`[bpmn]` renders BPMN 2.0 XML (the same format bpmn.io and most process-modeling tools export). Like `mermaid` and `excalidraw`, it needs its own headless-Chrome companion container — the bundled `kroki-compose.yml` already includes one:

```
[bpmn]
....
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<definitions xmlns="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
    xmlns:bpmndi="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI"
    xmlns:omgdc="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DC"
    xmlns:omgdi="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DI"
    id="definitions" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn">
  <process id="process_1" isExecutable="false">
    <startEvent id="start" name="Request received"/>
    <task id="task" name="Handle request"/>
    <endEvent id="end" name="Done"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="flow_1" sourceRef="start" targetRef="task"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="flow_2" sourceRef="task" targetRef="end"/>
  </process>
  <bpmndi:BPMNDiagram id="diagram">
    <bpmndi:BPMNPlane id="plane" bpmnElement="process_1">
      <bpmndi:BPMNShape id="start_di" bpmnElement="start">
        <omgdc:Bounds x="100" y="100" width="36" height="36"/>
      </bpmndi:BPMNShape>
      <bpmndi:BPMNShape id="task_di" bpmnElement="task">
        <omgdc:Bounds x="200" y="78" width="100" height="80"/>
      </bpmndi:BPMNShape>
      <bpmndi:BPMNShape id="end_di" bpmnElement="end">
        <omgdc:Bounds x="360" y="100" width="36" height="36"/>
      </bpmndi:BPMNShape>
      <bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="flow_1_di" bpmnElement="flow_1">
        <omgdi:waypoint x="136" y="118"/>
        <omgdi:waypoint x="200" y="118"/>
      </bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
      <bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="flow_2_di" bpmnElement="flow_2">
        <omgdi:waypoint x="300" y="118"/>
        <omgdi:waypoint x="360" y="118"/>
      </bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
    </bpmndi:BPMNPlane>
  </bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>
</definitions>
....
```

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>

<!DOCTYPE svg PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD SVG 1.1//EN" "http://www.w3.org/Graphics/SVG/1.1/DTD/svg11.dtd">

### Excalidraw

`[excalidraw]` renders an Excalidraw scene (the JSON a `.excalidraw` file, or [excalidraw.com](https://excalidraw.com)'s own "Save to…​" export, contains). Unlike `bpmn`, this type **does** need its own companion — the bundled `kroki-compose.yml` includes an `excalidraw` service alongside `mermaid` for exactly that reason:

```
[excalidraw]
....
{
  "type": "excalidraw",
  "version": 2,
  "elements": [
    {
      "type": "rectangle",
      "id": "rect1",
      "x": 100,
      "y": 100,
      "width": 200,
      "height": 100,
      "strokeColor": "#1e1e1e",
      "backgroundColor": "transparent",
      "seed": 1
    },
    {
      "type": "text",
      "id": "text1",
      "x": 130,
      "y": 135,
      "width": 140,
      "height": 25,
      "text": "Hello, Excalidraw",
      "fontSize": 20,
      "seed": 2
    }
  ]
}
....
```

## Inline macros: `label:` and `mono:`

```
label:grey[Default] label:red[Blocked] label:orange[Pending] label:green[Stable]
label:blue[Info] label:purple[Beta] label:pink[New] label:teal[Docs] label:white[White]

mono:[className]
```

Default Blocked Pending Stable Info Beta New Docs White

`mono:` is plain monospaced text with no code-chip styling — for a table cell whose entire content is a bare token (see [AsciiDoc basics](../reference-asciidoc-basics/)'s Tables section, which uses backtick code instead; `className` is the deliberate opt-out when a whole column of cells is tokens and the chip would be noise): `className`

## Table and video sizing attributes

`table-width=` and `nowrap-cols=` are demonstrated in [AsciiDoc basics](../reference-asciidoc-basics/)'s Tables section. The one remaining sizing attribute, for a video block, is not rendered live on this page (it would embed a real, unrelated third-party video) — the syntax is:

```
video::VIDEO_ID[youtube,640,360]
```

`640,360` both caps the embed’s width and locks its aspect ratio at any narrower viewport; width alone caps the width and leaves the ratio at the 16:9 fallback.

---

# Integrations

Source: /prerelease/main/reference-integrations/

Build-time and content capabilities that ship with every scaffolded site — as opposed to [UI Bundle](../reference-ui-bundle/)'s site chrome, or [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/)'s authoring blocks. Grouped by what they’re for.

## Authoring & content

### Diagrams — Kroki

`[mermaid]`, `[plantuml]`, `[graphviz]`, `[bpmn]`, `[excalidraw]` and more render as real diagrams via a self-hosted [Kroki](https://kroki.io) service, enabled by default (`kroki-enabled: true`, `kroki-diagram-types` in `antora-playbook.yml` — see [Antora Playbook](../reference-antora-playbook-configuration/)). The service starts itself automatically the first time a build needs it ([Docker](https://www.docker.com) required); `docouture teardown kroki` stops it, `docouture eject kroki` copies its compose definition out for customization. Mermaid diagrams get IOP Design System-aligned theming baked in server-side. `format=png` renders a transparent raster image instead of inline SVG for types that support it. Without Docker, or with the feature disabled, a diagram block renders as its own literal source text rather than failing the build. Full syntax: [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/).

### Syntax highlighting — Shiki

`source-highlighter: shiki` in `antora-playbook.yml` switches every code block from [Antora](https://antora.org)'s own client-side default ([highlight.js](https://highlightjs.org)) to build-time, static highlighting. `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions’ [Shiki](https://shiki.style) prewarm step builds the highlighter once up front rather than per-block.

### Changelog pages

[Changelog](../changelog/)'s per-version sections are generated at build time from
`code/CHANGELOG.md`, not hand-copied: `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` parses
every cut  [x.y.z] section, converts its `# Section` headings and - [PR](url)
text bullets to AsciiDoc, and appends each one as a `== vX.Y.Z` section directly onto
whatever page already lives at `changelog/index.adoc` — only on a site that has one; a
site with no changelog page is left untouched. `# [Unreleased]` is deliberately
excluded, the same way Keep a Changelog itself doesn’t consider it a version.

The file is read once per build, off disk, applied identically to every component version being built — not resolved per-ref through git, so a future build that aggregates two real docs versions side by side will show the same (current) changelog content on both until that gets revisited. Override the default `code/CHANGELOG.md` location (resolved relative to the playbook’s own directory) with `changelog_path` on the extension’s registration entry:

```
antora:
  extensions:
    - require: '@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions'
      changelog_path: ../code/CHANGELOG.md
```

## Discovery & search

### Full-text search

`@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` builds a search index at build time, published per component version, that the UI bundle’s search dialog reads directly ([UI Bundle](../reference-ui-bundle/)). No manual wiring — registering the extension is enough.

### AI ingestion — `llms.txt`

Every build publishes `llms.txt` (a Markdown index) and `llms-full.txt` (a full aggregated Markdown dump) at the site root, alongside `sitemap.xml` — the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org), letting an agent read the site without scraping rendered HTML. Configured under `docs/src/antora.yml’s `llms` key (see [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/)) — `summary` becomes the blockquote under the site title; `exclude` leaves specific pages out of both files. See also [AI-First approach](../reference-ai-first-approach/) for the broader philosophy this feeds into.

## Site reliability & URLs

### External link checking

A scaffolded site ships `scripts/check-links.mjs` (via [linkinator](https://github.com/JustinBeckwith/linkinator)) and a `check-links` [npm](https://www.npmjs.com) script. `package.json’s own `docouture.checkLinks.ignore` is a list of URL globs to skip — pre-seeded with this repository’s own URL, so a build doesn’t fail checking a link to itself before it’s ever been published.

### URL routing: the `/latest/` alias

Rather than Antora’s own `urls.latest_version_segment` (whose default `replace` strategy turns one real version segment into a permanent redirect stub the moment a release exists — see [Versioning modes](../guides-versioning-modes/)), `duplicate_latest_version: true` on the `antora.extensions` registration entry republishes whichever version Antora computes as latest a **second** time, under `/latest/…`, as a genuinely independent copy — so both the real version segment and `/latest/` stay real content.

### Legacy URL redirects

For a site migrated from another documentation tool, arbitrary literal legacy URLs can redirect to whatever real page now answers the equivalent URL — configured as `from`/`to` URL templates on the `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` registration entry itself (not `antora.yml`, since these apply across every ref a build aggregates, not per-version):

```
antora:
  extensions:
    - require: '@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions'
      redirects:
        - from: '/docs/main/old-page'
          to: '/main/new-page'
        - from: '/docs/**'
          to: '/main/**'
```

`*` captures one path segment,  captures the remainder. Rules are first-match-wins
in authoring order — an exact override belongs ahead of a broad `` catch-all.

---

# Reference

Source: /prerelease/main/reference-overview/

What each piece of docouture actually is, not how to use it task-by-task — see [Guides](../guides-overview/) for the how-tos. Grouped by what it is:

- [Configuration](../reference-configuration/) — every key in the Antora playbook and the component descriptor, what it does.
- [CLI](../reference-cli/) — every `docouture` command, its arguments and flags.
- [UI Bundle](../reference-ui-bundle/) — the themed UI’s built-in chrome (theme, search, navigation, 404 page) and what of it is configurable.
- [AsciiDoc](../reference-asciidoc/) — the language itself, and this site’s own custom blocks, each with a live rendered example.
- [Integrations](../reference-integrations/) — diagrams, syntax highlighting, search, AI ingestion, link checking and URL routing, grouped by what they’re for.
- [AI-First approach](../reference-ai-first-approach/) — the philosophy behind treating docs as something an agent reads and writes, and the skill set that does it.

---

# UI Bundle

Source: /prerelease/main/reference-ui-bundle/

`@inditextech/docouture-ui-bundle` — a themed fork of [antora-ui-default](https://gitlab.com/antora/antora-ui-default), read by [Antora](https://antora.org) as a plain zip via `ui.bundle.url`. What follows is what a site actually gets from it, beyond styling — each feature below, plus a `Configuration` subsection wherever there’s actually a knob to turn.

## Theme: dark / light

A theme toggle persists the choice (localStorage), applied before first paint so there’s no flash of the wrong theme.

### Configuration

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `site.keys.product_logo` / `product_logo_dark` | Side-menu brand logo; the dark variant is swapped in automatically under dark mode — see [Setup the product logo](../guides-setup-the-product-logo/). |

## Navigation

- **Module switcher** — appears once a component has more than one entry in `nav_modules`; see [Adding a module](../guides-adding-a-module/).
- **Nav tree** — renders each module’s own `nav.adoc`.
- **Breadcrumbs** — derived from the navigation tree’s ancestors of the current page.
- **Pagination** — previous/next footer links, on by default site-wide; a page can opt out with `:!page-pagination:`.
- **"Edit this page"** — links to the content source’s edit URL, inferred for known git hosts.
- **Header repo link** — reads `site.keys.repo_url`, or falls back to the content source’s own git remote if that key isn’t set.

### Configuration

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `site.keys.repo_url` | Header toolbar repo link, overriding the git-remote fallback. |
| `asciidoc.attributes.page-pagination` | Turns pagination on/off site-wide (`'@'` as a soft default) — see [Antora Playbook](../reference-antora-playbook-configuration/). |
| `nav_modules` | Drives the module switcher — see [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/). |

## Table of contents

An "on this page" scrollspy TOC tracks the current section as you scroll. Heading anchors are clickable (`sectanchors`).

### Configuration

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `:page-role: -toc` | Page-level attribute suppressing the TOC on that one page. |
| `asciidoc.attributes.sectanchors` | Site-wide switch for clickable heading anchors. |

## Search

A search dialog reads the full-text search index `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` builds at build time (see [Integrations](../reference-integrations/)) — without that extension registered, the dialog renders but has nothing to search. Recent searches persist locally. Nothing else to configure beyond registering the extension.

## Version switcher

A version dropdown renders once a component has more than one version — see [Versioning modes](../guides-versioning-modes/). A single-version component (the common case before a first release) renders a plain version indicator instead of a dropdown. No UI-bundle-level configuration of its own — it follows directly from how many versions the playbook aggregates.

## 404 page

Antora’s own generated 404 page has no component/module context at all — no side menu, no version tag, no footer. `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` composes a real one instead, so every partial that reads page context renders exactly as it would on a real page.

### Configuration

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `not_found_module` | Which module’s navigation the generated 404 page’s side menu shows — see [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/). |

## Copy-to-clipboard

Every code block gets a copy button, regardless of whether it has a language set. No configuration.

## Bundle-wide settings

Keys that shape the bundle itself rather than one single feature above:

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `site.keys.favicon` | Browser tab icon — see [Setup a favicon](../guides-setup-a-favicon/). |
| `ui.bundle.url` / `snapshot` | Which bundle zip, and whether to cache it. |
| `ui.supplemental_files` | Overlay directory for the logo/favicon files above. |
| `ui.default_layout` | Layout for pages with no `page-layout` attribute (default `default`). |
| `ui.output_dir` | Where UI assets land inside the site (default `_`). |

---

# Structure

Source: /prerelease/main/structure/

docouture is an [Nx](https://nx.dev)/https://pnpm.io[pnpm] monorepo. What a scaffolded site actually depends on is a small slice of it — the rest is how docouture itself is built.

| Path | What’s there |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/cli` | `@inditextech/docouture-cli` — the `docouture` binary. Bundles its own scaffolding template (`templates/starter`) and [GitHub](https://github.com/features/actions) workflow templates (`templates/workflows`). |
| `packages/ui-bundle` | `@inditextech/docouture-ui-bundle` — the themed [Antora](https://antora.org) UI, built to a zip (`build/ui-bundle-<version>.zip` plus an unversioned alias). |
| `packages/antora-extensions` | `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` — the Antora pipeline extensions (module switcher, footer, search index, llms.txt, [Kroki](https://kroki.io)/https://shiki.style[Shiki] prewarm, redirects). |
| `packages/asciidoc-extensions` | `@inditextech/docouture-asciidoc-extensions` — the [Asciidoctor](https://asciidoctor.org) content extensions (tabs, cards, accordion, feature-tabs, cta, label/mono macros, Kroki, Shiki). |
| `packages/publish-gh-pages` | `@inditextech/docouture-publish-gh-pages` — the `docouture publish gh-pages` driver. |
| `packages/tooling` | Internal workspace tooling (release bumps, changelog checks, a local snapshot registry) — not something a scaffolded site ever depends on. |

## What a scaffolded site actually contains

`docouture new` writes into the **target** repository, not into this one:

```
docs/
  antora-playbook.yml               real build (main + stable/version tags)
  antora-playbook.local.yml         HEAD-only build, used by `docouture dev` and PR checks
  package.json                      devDependencies: the CLI, ui-bundle, both extension
                                     packages, the gh-pages publish driver, antora itself
  src/
    antora.yml                      component descriptor: name, title, version, nav
    modules/
      ROOT/pages/index.adoc         the landing page only
      main/nav.adoc                 the navigation tree
      main/pages/*.adoc             every other page
.github/workflows/docouture-*.yml   PR verification, prerelease/release publish, release cutting
AGENTS.md                           docouture's own managed section, merged into whatever
                                     was already there
```

This site you’re reading is exactly that shape — see it directly at [`docs/` on `main`](https://github.com/InditexTech/docouture/tree/main/docs).

---

# Changelog

Source: /prerelease/main/changelog/

docouture’s own changelog is `code/CHANGELOG.md` in the [source repository](https://github.com/InditexTech/docouture) — the unabridged, [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)-format record, grouped into Added/Fixed/Documentation/Deprecated/Removed/Security sections under an `## [Unreleased]` heading until a version is actually cut.

In contrast, [Release notes](../release-notes/) summarizes what matters to **users** of a given release, not every commit-level entry.

## Convention

Every entry is `- [#PR_ID](PR_URL) PR_NAME`, linking the pull request that shipped the change (not a tracking issue). Not every merged PR gets one — a PR labelled `skip-release`, or carrying only an internal/epic label with no real user-facing category, is intentionally left out.

> **Tip**
> `[Unreleased]` — what’s landed but not yet cut into a release — is never mirrored
> here; see `code/CHANGELOG.md` directly for that. Every **cut** version below, though, is
> generated straight from that same file at build time, so it can’t drift from it.

## Versions

No tagged release yet — see `code/CHANGELOG.md’s `[Unreleased]` section for what has landed so far.

# v1.0.0 (illustrative)

Source: /prerelease/main/release-notes/1-0-0/

> **Note**
> Illustrative — docouture has no tagged release yet (still `0.1.0`, see [Release notes](../)). This is what a first stable release summary would say about what already exists in the repository today, written ahead of an actual `v1.0.0` tag.

docouture turns "we should really document this" into a real, versioned documentation site in minutes, not weeks — scaffolded straight into the repository the product it documents already lives in, themed with Inditex’s own design system, and built to be written and kept in sync by AI agents just as easily as by hand.

## Ship a site, not a project

One command, `docouture new`, is the whole setup: a full [Antora](https://antora.org) content tree, [GitHub](https://github.com/features/actions) workflows, and an `AGENTS.md` briefing so an AI agent can pick up the site immediately — dropped into an existing repository, interactively or with flags, in one pass. `docouture dev` serves it with live reload while writing; `docouture build`, `publish`, `doctor`, `upgrade`, `eject`, `teardown` and `completion` cover everything from there to a published site and back. See [CLI](../../reference-cli/).

## Grow it the way the project actually grows

Every site picks its own versioning story from day one: a rolling **standalone** stable prerelease pair for a product that only ever needs "the current docs", or a full **versioned** history where every release keeps its own docs forever. Either way, nothing about how pages are written changes — only how many copies of them the site ends up publishing. See [Versioning modes](../../guides-versioning-modes/).

## Look like the product, not like a template

The UI bundle is a themed fork of Antora’s own default UI on top of Inditex’s IOP Design System: dark/light mode, a version switcher, full-text search that needs no extra wiring, and a set of authoring blocks — `[tabs]`, `[cards]`, `[accordion]`, `[feature-tabs]`, `[cta]` — for the parts of a page plain [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org) was never going to express on its own.

## Content that does more than sit still

Diagrams render for real — [Kroki](https://kroki.io)-backed mermaid, plantuml, bpmn and excalidraw — code blocks get build-time [Shiki](https://shiki.style) syntax highlighting instead of a client-side afterthought, and every build produces [`llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org)/`llms-full.txt` so an AI agent can read the site as plainly as a person can. External link checking catches rot before it ships. See [Integrations](../../reference-integrations/).

## Publish and move on

`docouture publish gh-pages` — a CNAME custom-domain option and automatic `.nojekyll` handling included — is the entire path from a finished build to a live URL. See [Publishing a documentation](../../guides-publishing-a-documentation/).

---

# Architecture

Source: /1.0.0/main/architecture/

docouture turns a git repository into a themed [Antora](https://antora.org) documentation site. It has no engine of its own — it wires together an existing content pipeline (Antora), a themed UI, two sets of build-time extensions, and a CLI that scaffolds and drives all of it. Each piece is independently replaceable: swap the UI bundle, drop an extension package, or skip the CLI and call Antora directly. The sections below cover each piece, then how a build actually strings them together.

## The content pipeline: Antora

Antora aggregates [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org) content from one or more git repositories/refs into a single site, based on a **playbook** (`antora-playbook.yml`) and one **component descriptor** (`antora.yml`) per documentation component. docouture doesn’t replace Antora’s model — it generates a playbook and descriptor that already point at the right things, and layers extensions on top. See [Antora’s own documentation](https://docs.antora.org/antora/latest/) for the model itself, and [Antora Playbook](../reference-antora-playbook-configuration/)/ [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/) for what this site’s own copies of those two files say.

## The UI: a themed Antora UI bundle

`@inditextech/docouture-ui-bundle` is a themed fork of [antora-ui-default](https://gitlab.com/antora/antora-ui-default): Handlebars layouts and partials, CSS built on the IOP Design System’s tokens, and browser scripts for theme switching, search, tabs, accordions and the on-page table of contents. Antora reads it as a plain zip (`ui.bundle.url` in the playbook) — nothing about it is docouture-specific from Antora’s point of view. See [UI Bundle](../reference-ui-bundle/).

## The extensions: two different seams

Two packages hook two different parts of the pipeline, registered under two different playbook keys:

- `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` (`antora.extensions`) — site-level behavior: it hooks Antora’s own site-generation pipeline to add things Antora doesn’t do on its own — the module switcher, the site footer, the search index, `llms.txt` generation, the [Kroki](https://kroki.io)/https://shiki.style[Shiki] prewarm steps, legacy URL redirects, and the `/latest/` alias.
- `@inditextech/docouture-asciidoc-extensions` (`asciidoc.extensions`) — page-level content: it hooks the [Asciidoctor](https://asciidoctor.org) processor itself to add AsciiDoc syntax docouture sites can write that stock Asciidoctor doesn’t have — `[tabs]`, `[cards]`, `[accordion]`, `[feature-tabs]`, `[cta]`, the `label:`/`mono:` macros, table/video sizing attributes, and the Kroki/Shiki block implementations.

Listing either package under the other’s key makes Antora log a warning and skip it — see [Antora Playbook](../reference-antora-playbook-configuration/).

## The CLI: scaffolding, not a build tool

`docouture` (`@inditextech/docouture-cli`) doesn’t build anything itself — `docouture build`/`dev` are thin wrappers around Antora, and `docouture publish` resolves a publish driver package (`@inditextech/docouture-publish-<target>`) from the site’s own `node_modules`. What the CLI actually owns:

| Responsibility | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| Scaffolding | `new` |
| Build (wraps Antora, doesn’t replace it) | `build`, `dev` |
| Publishing (resolves a `docouture-publish-<target>` driver) | `publish` |
| Version bookkeeping | `version` |
| Diagnostics | `doctor` |
| Re-syncing generated files | `upgrade`, `eject`, `teardown` |

See [CLI](../reference-cli/).

## How a build actually runs

Locally, `docouture build`/`dev` shells out to the site’s own `npm run build` (`antora --fetch antora-playbook.yml`). Antora aggregates content from `content.sources[]`, applies `asciidoc.extensions` to every page, then runs `antora.extensions` over the resulting site model, and the UI bundle renders it through its Handlebars layouts.

In CI it’s the same pipeline through one of the workflows `docouture new` scaffolds, differing only in which playbook they read and what happens after:

- **`docouture-pr-verify.yml`** — every pull request, builds `antora-playbook.local.yml` (HEAD only — no other ref is reachable from a PR checkout), then runs link checking. Never publishes.
- **`docouture-publish-prerelease.yml`** — every push to `main` that touches content, builds the real `antora-playbook.yml`, then calls `docouture-publish.yml` (`docouture publish <target>`, pushing whatever lands at `output.dir`) to publish it.
- **`docouture-release.yml`** — cutting a release, tags the version, then also calls `docouture-publish.yml` for the definitive post-release build.

See [Publishing a documentation](../guides-publishing-a-documentation/) and [Releasing a documentation](../guides-releasing-a-documentation/) for each workflow’s own triggers.

---

# Contributing

Source: /1.0.0/main/contributing/

docouture is developed at [InditexTech/docouture](https://github.com/InditexTech/docouture). Contributions there follow the repository’s own guide, not this scaffolded site’s — the summary below is what actually applies; see `CONTRIBUTING.md` in that repository for the full text.

## Before contributing

- Sign the [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](https://github.com/InditexTech/foss/blob/main/CLA.md) — required before any code contribution is accepted.
- Install `just`, `asdf`, and the pinned [Node](https://nodejs.org)/https://pnpm.io[pnpm] versions the repository’s own `README.md` documents.

## Workflow

1. Open an issue to discuss the change first.
2. Fork, branch, and make the change.
3. Run `just check` (lint, typecheck, formatting — what CI runs).
4. Update `code/CHANGELOG.md’s `[Unreleased]` section — required on every PR touching `code/**`, unless labelled `skip-release` for a change with no user-facing effect.
5. Open a pull request linking the issue.

## Contributing to this site specifically

If what needs fixing is a page under `docs/` (this site, not docouture itself), that’s a normal docs PR against whatever repository this site was scaffolded into — see [Adding a page](../guides-adding-a-page/) for the mechanics, and [AI-First approach](../reference-ai-first-approach/)'s `docouture-documenting-changes` skill for keeping content in sync as the underlying repo changes.

## License

Apache-2.0, except `packages/ui-bundle` (a fork of [antora-ui-default](https://gitlab.com/antora/antora-ui-default)), which remains MPL-2.0 under its own LICENSE/NOTICE.

---

# FAQ

Source: /1.0.0/main/faq/

1. What is docouture?

A documentation platform: a themed [Antora](https://antora.org) UI bundle (IOP Design System), a set of Antora/https://asciidoctor.org[Asciidoctor] extensions, and the `docouture` CLI that scaffolds, serves, builds and publishes a site on top of them. See [About](../).

2. Do I need to know Antora or AsciiDoc already?

Only the basics of [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org) for writing pages — the CLI scaffolds everything else (playbook, component descriptor, navigation, workflows). See [Quickstart](../quickstart/).

3. How do I create a new site?

`npx @inditextech/docouture-cli new <name>` from an existing git repository. See [Quickstart](../quickstart/) and [CLI](../reference-cli/).

4. Can documentation be versioned?

Yes — standalone (a rolling stable tag alongside a prerelease) or versioned (every release its own immutable tag, kept forever). See [Versioning modes](../guides-versioning-modes/).

5. Does it support diagrams?

Yes, via a self-hosted [Kroki](https://kroki.io) service: mermaid, plantuml, bpmn, excalidraw and more, enabled by default. See [Integrations](../reference-integrations/).

6. What about syntax highlighting?

Build-time, via [Shiki](https://shiki.style) — set with `source-highlighter: shiki` in the playbook, already the default a scaffolded site ships with.

7. Is search included?

Yes — a full-text search index is built at build time and read directly by the UI bundle’s own search dialog, no extra wiring required.

8. How do I publish the site?

`docouture publish gh-pages`, or the [GitHub](https://github.com/features/actions) workflows `docouture new` already scaffolds. See [Publishing a documentation](../guides-publishing-a-documentation/).

9. Can AI agents help write the docs?

Yes — `npx skills@latest add InditexTech/docouture --all` installs a set of agent skills that plan structure, draft content from the repo, and keep it in sync as the repo changes. See [AI-First approach](../reference-ai-first-approach/).

10. Is docouture open source?

The CLI, the Antora/Asciidoctor extensions and the release tooling are Apache-2.0 (the UI bundle’s own fork of [antora-ui-default](https://gitlab.com/antora/antora-ui-default) remains MPL-2.0, per its own LICENSE). The UI bundle is themed with Inditex’s proprietary IOP Design System, though, which is **not** open source — a site built with this UI bundle is internal-only until that changes, regardless of the code’s own license.

---

# Glossary

Source: /1.0.0/main/glossary/

## Component

An [Antora](https://antora.org) unit of documentation: a directory with its own `antora.yml`, one or more `modules/`, and (optionally) several **versions**. A scaffolded site starts with exactly one component.

## Module

A subdivision of a component with its own `nav.adoc` and `pages/` tree. A scaffolded site starts with two: `ROOT` (the landing page only) and `main` (everything else).

## Playbook

`antora-playbook.yml` — Antora’s single entry-point config file: which content to aggregate, which UI bundle to use, and which [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org)/Antora extensions to load. See [Antora Playbook](../reference-antora-playbook-configuration/).

## Component descriptor

`antora.yml` (this site’s own lives at `docs/src/antora.yml`) — a component’s name, title, version, navigation list, and the docouture-specific keys (`nav_modules`/`footer`/`llms`/`not_found_module`) that `@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions` reads. See [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/).

## Resource ID

How Antora addresses content — `version@component:module:family$relative/path.adoc`, most of which defaults to the current page’s own context. `Quickstart` is a resource ID, not a file path.

## Standalone / Versioned

The two versioning modes `docouture new --mode` offers, decided once at scaffold time. Standalone keeps `main` as a permanent **prerelease** build and moves a single rolling `stable` tag on each release — no historical archive, only "now" and "what’s next". Versioned keeps `main` as prerelease too, but gives every release its own immutable `vX.Y.Z` tag forever, plus a `docs/.release-version` file tracking the next release’s target version — appropriate when old releases (an SDK, a CLI) must keep resolving unchanged after a new one ships. See [Versioning modes](../guides-versioning-modes/).

## Antora extension

A package registered under the playbook’s `antora.extensions` key — it hooks Antora’s own site-generation pipeline, running over the whole aggregated site model rather than a single page. This is where docouture’s module switcher, site footer, search index, `llms.txt` generation, Kroki/Shiki prewarm steps, legacy URL redirects and the `/latest/` alias live (`@inditextech/docouture-antora-extensions`). See [Architecture](../architecture/).

## Asciidoctor extension

A package registered under the playbook’s `asciidoc.extensions` key — it hooks the [Asciidoctor](https://asciidoctor.org) content processor itself, running per-page during AsciiDoc conversion. This is where docouture’s custom syntax lives — `[tabs]`, `[cards]`, `[accordion]`, `[feature-tabs]`, `[cta]`, the `label:`/`mono:` macros, table/video sizing attributes, and the Kroki/Shiki block implementations (`@inditextech/docouture-asciidoc-extensions`). Listing it under `antora.extensions` instead (or vice versa) makes Antora log a warning and skip it. See [Architecture](../architecture/).

## Publish driver

The package a publish target resolves to: named `@inditextech/docouture-publish-<target>`, looked up in the site’s own `node_modules` when `docouture publish <target>` runs. It does the actual work of getting a built site live — for `gh-pages`, the only driver docouture ships today, that means pushing `output.dir` to a `gh-pages` branch, plus fixes the bare `gh-pages` npm package doesn’t provide on its own: a default `github-actions[bot]` git identity, surfaced failures instead of silent ones, a clean orphan first commit, and an always-written `.nojekyll`. See [Publishing a documentation](../guides-publishing-a-documentation/).

---

# Adding a module

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-adding-a-module/

A scaffolded site starts with two modules: `ROOT` (the landing page only) and `main` (everything else). Add a module when a section of the site earns its own switchable navigation, rather than living grouped inside `main`.

## 1. Create the module’s tree

```
docs/src/modules/<name>/
  nav.adoc
  pages/
```

## 2. List it in `docs/src/antora.yml`

Add its `nav.adoc` alongside `main’s own entry — never remove `main’s:

```
nav:
  - modules/main/nav.adoc
  - modules/<name>/nav.adoc
```

## 3. Describe it under `nav_modules`

A **list**, not a map — see [Antora Descriptor](../reference-antora-descriptor-configuration/) for why a map silently breaks a hyphenated module slug:

```
nav_modules:
  - module: main
    title: Documentation
    description: The core product story.
    icon: design/grid-outlined
  - module: <name>
    title: <Title>
    description: One-line description of this module.
    icon: <group>/<name>
```

Once a second entry exists, the UI’s module switcher appears automatically — with just one module, there’s nothing to switch between.

`icon` is `<group>/<name>` from the UI bundle’s own vendored sprite, not a free-form name — see [Icon gallery](../guides-icon-gallery/) for every icon this site’s UI bundle ships.

---

# Adding a page

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-adding-a-page/

Create an [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org) file under a module’s `pages/` directory, then add it to that module’s `nav.adoc` so it’s reachable:

```
* xref:my-new-page.adoc[My new page]
```

A page not listed in `nav.adoc` still builds and publishes at its own URL — it’s just unreachable by browsing, and gets no breadcrumbs/previous-next pagination.

## Group without a page of its own

A bare list item with no `xref:` starts a new, unlinked heading in the side menu — this is how [Modifying the navigation](../guides-modifying-the-navigation/)'s section grouping works, and how this site’s own `main:nav.adoc` groups Overview/Getting started/Guides/Reference/etc.:

```
* Getting started
* xref:main:prerequisites.adoc[Prerequisites]
* xref:main:quickstart.adoc[Quickstart]
```

## Writing the page itself

See [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/) for the blocks this site’s UI bundle adds on top of plain AsciiDoc (tabs, cards, accordions, feature-tabs, cta), and the `docouture-writing-docs-pages` agent skill’s `reference/language-basics.md` for plain AsciiDoc itself — headings, lists, tables, code blocks, admonitions, cross-references.

---

# Content &amp; structure

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-content-structure/

How a scaffolded site’s shape grows over time: new modules, new pages within them, and the `nav.adoc` list that makes both reachable from the side menu.

- [Adding a module](../guides-adding-a-module/) — when a section of the site earns its own switchable navigation instead of living grouped inside `main`.
- [Adding a page](../guides-adding-a-page/) — create an AsciiDoc file under a module’s `pages/` directory and wire it into that module’s `nav.adoc`.
- [Modifying the navigation](../guides-modifying-the-navigation/) — `nav.adoc’s list syntax: nesting by depth, linked vs. unlinked items.
- [Icon gallery](../guides-icon-gallery/) — every icon this site’s UI bundle ships, and which ones actually render in a `[card,icon=]`.

# Icon gallery

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-icon-gallery/

Every icon this site’s UI bundle actually ships, so you never have to guess a `group/name` string and find out only after a card renders with a blank header slot.

The set below is fixed by whichever `@inditextech/docouture-ui-bundle` version this site depends on — a normal site cannot add to it. The icons come from Inditex’s proprietary internal design-system mirror; the fetch/build tooling that vendors them (`src/img/icons.yml`, `just icons-fetch`/`icons-build`) only runs inside the `docouture` monorepo itself, against an internal asset host. Need one that isn’t here? Open a request against the `docouture` repository — there’s no way to add it from a site that just depends on the published bundle.

## Two places an icon reference is read, two different rules

- `nav_modules[].icon` (see [Adding a module](../guides-adding-a-module/)) is resolved by a Handlebars helper at **page-render** time, with full access to the icon sprite — any icon in this gallery works there, both sections below.
- `[card,icon="group/name"]` (see [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/)) is resolved by the Asciidoctor extension itself at **build** time, which has no access to the sprite at all — it can only emit a pre-generated CSS class. Only the icons in the first section below have one. Reference one from the second section instead, and nothing errors — the card just renders with an empty icon slot, silently.

## Usable in `[card,icon=]`

Every icon here has a generated CSS mask, so it’s guaranteed to actually render in a card’s header. Copy the `group/name` string as-is.

## Vendored, but not card-safe

These exist in the sprite and work fine in `nav_modules[].icon`, but have no CSS mask — putting one in `[card,icon=]` renders no icon and no warning.

| --- | --- |
| `accessibility/moon-outlined` | Dark-mode icon on the light/dark theme toggle. |
| `actions/add-outlined` | Vendored; no current template use in this bundle version. |
| `actions/back-outlined` | Vendored; no current template use in this bundle version. |
| `actions/close-large-outlined` | Side-menu drawer’s close button (mobile breakpoint). |
| `actions/close-small-outlined` | A recent-search entry’s remove button. |

# Landing page modifications

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-landing-page-modifications/

The landing page (`ROOT/pages/index.adoc`) is the one page rendered through the UI bundle’s `home` layout (`:page-layout: home`). The layout itself builds only the hero — everything below it is the page’s own ordinary AsciiDoc body, using blocks that happen to have no plain-AsciiDoc equivalent. Its section order is therefore fixed — each block is optional, but present blocks appear in this order:

1. **Hero** — the page’s own header attributes.
2. **Get started** — a `[cards]` block, typically 4 entry points.
3. **Key features** — a `[feature-tabs]` block, a handful of capability slides.
4. **A CTA** — a `[cta]` block, one pitch plus one action.
5. **FAQ** — an `[accordion]` block.

`:page-nav-module: main` is what gives the landing page a side menu at all — `ROOT` itself has no `nav.adoc`, so it borrows whichever module this attribute names.

Every block below is documented in full syntax in [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/) — this page is what’s actually editable on **this** landing page and what each change does, not the block reference.

## Hero

Set as page attributes on `index.adoc` itself, not a block:

```
:description: One sentence, used as the page's meta description only — it is not
              shown anywhere in the hero itself.
:page-tags: antora, cli, design-system
:page-action: Get started
:page-action-url: main:quickstart.adoc
:page-action-secondary: About
:page-action-secondary-url: main:index.adoc
:page-hero-image: hero-placeholder.png
:page-hero-image-alt: A one-line description of the image, for screen readers.
```

- `:description:` is meta-only on the `home` layout — unlike the default page layout’s hero, it never renders as a visible subtitle. Write it for search engines and link-preview cards, not as landing-page copy.
- `:page-tags:` is a comma-separated list, rendered as chips under the title.
- `:page-action:`/`:page-action-url:` is the primary button — **both halves are required**; set only one and neither renders (a button that goes nowhere is worse than no button).
- `:page-action-secondary:`/`:page-action-secondary-url:` is the same rule, and it’s nested inside the primary action’s markup — if the primary pair is unset, the secondary button doesn’t render either, even with both of its own halves set.
- `:page-hero-image:`/`:page-hero-image-alt:` is optional — the hero renders fine as text-only with no image. There’s no dark-mode variant for it (unlike feature/CTA images); pick artwork that reads on both themes, or skip it.
- `:page-hero-video:`/`:page-hero-video-poster:` is the same media slot, for a video instead of an image — if both `:page-hero-image:` and `:page-hero-video:` are set, the video wins.

## Get started

The site’s own real example:

```
[cards,type=image-square,columns="1 s:2 m:4",width=container]
====
[card,subheader="Start here"]
.xref:main:quickstart.adoc[Quickstart]
--
image::card-placeholder.png[Placeholder card image]

Scaffold a site and see it running locally in a few commands.
--
====
```

What each attribute changes:

- `type=` — `no-image` (default, text-only), `image-landscape`, `image-square`, or `image-portrait`. An unknown value warns and falls back to `no-image`.
- `columns=` — space-separated `breakpoint:count` tokens (bare `count` = the base/ mobile column count); breakpoints are `s`, `m`, `l` only, max 4 columns per breakpoint. Defaults to `"1 s:2 m:3"` if omitted.
- `width=` — `content` (default, matches the page’s text measure) or `container` (full page width — what this site’s own Get started section uses).
- Per-card `subheader=` and `icon=` share one header row and can be combined — they are not alternatives to each other, despite how the two examples in [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/) read side by side. `icon=` only accepts a `group/name` string with a working CSS mask — see [Icon gallery](../guides-icon-gallery/) for which ones actually render.
- Per-card `labels=` is a comma-separated list rendered as small grey chips, separate from `subheader=`.

Adding, removing or reordering a card is just adding, removing or reordering a `[card]` block inside the `====`; there’s no fixed count (4 is this template’s starting point, not a limit).

## Key features

Each `[feature]` is one tab. At least one of `label=` (the tab’s own text) or `.Title` (a heading shown in the panel) is required — set both when the tab label and the in-panel heading should read differently, set just one otherwise:

```
[feature,label="Scaffold in one command"]
--
image::feature-placeholder.png[Placeholder feature image]
image::feature-placeholder-dark.png[role=dark]

Prose for this slide.

[.cta]
xref:main:quickstart.adoc[Try it]
--
```

The `role=dark` image is optional but recommended whenever the light one wouldn’t read on a dark background — it’s swapped in automatically under the dark theme. The `[.cta]` link is optional and limited to one per slide (a second one is dropped, not an error). Regardless of the order these are authored in, a slide always renders as media, then prose, then the call to action.

Add, remove or reorder slides the same way as cards — one `[feature]` block per tab, no fixed count.

## A CTA

One pitch, one `[.primary]` action — and, less commonly needed, one `[.secondary]` action alongside it:

```
[cta]
====
A short pitch.

[.primary]
https://github.com/InditexTech/docouture[View the repository]

[.secondary]
xref:main:faq.adoc[Read the FAQ]
====
```

`align=` (`center`, the default, or `start`) controls whether the pitch and actions centre or left-align. `title=` adds a second, larger heading line inside the band itself — most callers don’t need it, since the `==` heading above the block (`Free & open source` on this site) already does that job.

## FAQ

Add or remove a question by adding or removing a `[%collapsible]` item inside the `[accordion]` block — see [Custom AsciiDoc components](../reference-custom-asciidoc-components/) for the `[%collapsible]` syntax itself. `%single-open` (an option on the `[accordion]` block, not this site’s current setting) closes whichever other item was open when a new one is expanded; without it, items toggle independently, which is what this landing page actually uses.

## A different layout shape

`:page-layout: home` (two-column: hero as a fixed side column, everything else scrolling in the main column) is one of two shipped landing shapes. `:page-layout: home-single` renders the identical hero and body content stacked in a single column instead — same attributes, same blocks, just a different arrangement. Switching is a one-line change on `index.adoc` itself.

## Replacing the placeholder images

`ROOT/images/{hero,card,feature,feature-dark}-placeholder.png` are stand-ins. Replace them with real artwork under the same filenames (or update the `image::` references to new ones) — they’re a separate concern from the **site** logo/favicon, which [Setup the product logo](../guides-setup-the-product-logo/) and [Setup a favicon](../guides-setup-a-favicon/) cover.

---

# Modifying the navigation

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-modifying-the-navigation/

Each module’s `nav.adoc` is a plain [AsciiDoc](https://asciidoc.org) unordered list.
Nesting is list depth
(, , ``); a linked item is `xref:page.adoc[Title]`; an unlinked item starts a
new, unlinked heading in the side menu:

```
* Overview
* xref:main:index.adoc[About]
* xref:main:architecture.adoc[Architecture]
* Getting started
* xref:main:prerequisites.adoc[Prerequisites]
* xref:main:quickstart.adoc[Quickstart]
```

This is exactly how this site’s own `main:nav.adoc` groups Overview / Getting started / Guides / Reference / Additional information / Contributing — six headings, none of them a page of their own, each grouping a run of real pages underneath it.

## The four names a rename has to keep in agreement

Renaming a component (not just adding/removing nav entries) touches four places that all have to agree, or the site builds with zero pages — `docouture doctor` checks all four:

| Name | Set in |
| --- | --- |
| Component name | `docs/src/antora.yml` → `name` |
| Start page | `antora-playbook.yml` → `site.start_page’s `<component>::` prefix |
| Content path | `antora-playbook.yml` → `content.sources[0].start_path` |
| Package name | `docs/package.json` → `name` (not load-bearing for [Antora](https://antora.org), but drift here usually means something else drifted too) |

## Adding a new module’s navigation

Covered separately in [Adding a module](../guides-adding-a-module/) — a new module needs both a `nav.adoc` of its own **and** an entry in `docs/src/antora.yml’s top-level `nav:` list and `nav_modules:`.

# Publishing a documentation

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-publishing-a-documentation/

`docouture new` already scaffolds two workflows that build the site and run `docouture publish gh-pages`:

- **`docouture-publish-prerelease.yml`** — runs on every ordinary push to `main` that touches docs content, no label needed. Keeps the prerelease version current.
- **`docouture-publish.yml`** — not triggered by push; `docouture-release.yml` calls it directly once a release is cut, and it’s also available for a manual rebuild+republish via its own `workflow_dispatch`.

Before either actually publishes anything, see [Prerequisites](../prerequisites/) for the repository/https://pages.github.com[GitHub Pages] side (public repository, `gh-pages` branch selected in Settings → Pages, the `docs/release` label created), plus:

1. `@inditextech/docouture-publish-gh-pages` in `devDependencies` — already present in the scaffolded `package.json`.
2. `site.url` set in `antora-playbook.yml` to the site’s real public URL — for a GitHub Pages project page, `https://<org>.github.io/<repo>` (the repo name has to be baked in as a path segment, or generated asset URLs come out wrong).

## Publishing manually

- pnpm
- npm

```
$ pnpm run build
$ pnpm exec docouture publish gh-pages
```

```
$ npm run build
$ npx docouture publish gh-pages
```

`GITHUB_TOKEN` (set automatically inside the [Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) workflow) authenticates the push; running this locally needs a token of your own with `repo` scope, passed as the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable.

## A custom domain

A `cname` string under `package.json’s own `docouture.publish.gh-pages` block — `docouture publish` writes it as a `CNAME` file alongside the built site:

```
{
  "docouture": {
    "publish": {
      "gh-pages": {
        "cname": "docs.example.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave the block empty, as scaffolded, for a plain `github.io` URL.

## `.nojekyll` — not optional

`@inditextech/docouture-publish-gh-pages` writes a `.nojekyll` file at the published
branch’s root regardless of configuration. Without it, GitHub Pages' own Jekyll
processing silently drops every -prefixed path — exactly where the UI bundle’s own
assets live (`//css/…​`, `/_/js/…​`) — and the published site loads unstyled. Pass
`"nojekyll": false` in that same `package.json` block only if something else genuinely
needs Jekyll on.

## What the driver fixes for you

`@inditextech/docouture-publish-gh-pages` wraps the underlying `gh-pages` package with three fixes: a default `github-actions[bot]` git identity (a fresh CI runner has none), surfacing failures the underlying package would otherwise swallow silently, and pre-creating the target branch as a clean orphan commit on first publish (avoiding a dirty first commit inherited from `main`).

---

# Releasing a documentation

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-releasing-a-documentation/

A release is cut by running `.github/workflows/docouture-release.yml` (scaffolded by `docouture new`), not by hand-editing anything under `docs/`. Two triggers:

- **Manually** — Actions tab → "docouture-release" → Run workflow. Works immediately.
- **Automatically** — merge a pull request into `main` carrying the `docs/release` label. That label isn’t created automatically — see [Prerequisites](../prerequisites/) — so until it exists, only the manual trigger works; a merge without it is a silent no-op, not an error.

Under the hood: `docouture version <value>` patches `docs/src/antora.yml` on a one-off commit built on `main’s current tip, `git tag v<value>` is created there, and the tag is pushed — `main` itself is never advanced.

## Standalone mode

Every release retargets the same `stable` tag — force-moved, not appended to. Nothing to set beforehand; the workflow’s default input is fine.

## Versioned mode

The target version comes from `docs/.release-version`, not a form field, when triggered by a labelled PR merge:

1. Edit `docs/.release-version` to the target version (e.g. `1.0.0`)
2. Open a PR with that change, labelled `docs/release`
3. Merge it — the workflow tags `v1.0.0`, then bumps the file forward to the next patch version so it’s always ready for whatever comes next

(Or skip the PR: run the workflow manually via `workflow_dispatch` and type the version directly — its form field is what a versioned-mode release actually requires there, unlike standalone’s, where the default is fine.)

## `docouture version` vs. a real release

`docouture version <value>` is the narrower tool the workflow itself calls internally — it only rewrites `docs/src/antora.yml’s `version:`/`prerelease:` fields in place. Useful for local, throwaway testing of how a version renders; it does not cut a release on either mode, and never touches `docs/.release-version`:

```
$ docouture version 1.0.0
$ docouture version 1.1.0-rc.0 --prerelease
```

## Every release tag is force-recreated

Republishing an already-released version (fixing a docs typo caught after the tag went out) is a deliberate, ordinary act — no separate flag needed. The one difference: the `docs/.release-version` forward-bump step is skipped on a republish, since that file’s current value was typically already the next planned target.

---

# Setup a favicon

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-setup-a-favicon/

The browser tab icon is a `site.keys.favicon` value in `antora-playbook.yml`, served from a file under `ui.supplemental_files`:

```
site:
  keys:
    favicon: /_/favicon.ico

ui:
  supplemental_files: ./supplemental-ui
```

`docouture new` already wires this up with a placeholder — replace
`docs/supplemental-ui/favicon.ico` with a real one, same filename, and rebuild. The
// prefix is the UI bundle’s own output directory (`ui.output_dir`, default ``),
not the site root — supplemental files land there, which is why the key isn’t just
`/favicon.ico`.

## What actually reads at that size

A favicon renders at 16–32px in a browser tab — full logo artwork (fine detail, gradients, a wordmark) turns to mush at that size. Use a flat, single-colour simplified mark instead: the product symbol alone (drop any text), filled solid in black, white, or the brand’s own solid accent — no gradients, no thin strokes. The seeded placeholder is a multi-res `.ico` (16×16 + 32×32 embedded); that’s still the safest container since browsers pick whichever embedded size fits, though a plain PNG works too — `head-icons.hbs` only ever emits a single `<link rel="icon">`, regardless of format.

## Using a different filename

Rename the file under `supplemental-ui/` and update `site.keys.favicon` to match — the path is a literal, not a convention [Antora](https://antora.org) infers.

## Removing it entirely

Delete the `favicon` key (and the file, if nothing else in `supplemental-ui/` references it) — the UI bundle falls back to no favicon rather than failing the build.

---

# Setup the product logo

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-setup-the-product-logo/

The side-menu brand mark next to the site title is `site.keys.product_logo` (and, for the dark theme, `product_logo_dark`), served the same way the favicon is — from `ui.supplemental_files`:

```
site:
  keys:
    product_logo: /_/product-logo.png
    product_logo_dark: /_/product-logo-dark.png

ui:
  supplemental_files: ./supplemental-ui
```

`docouture new` seeds both keys with placeholder artwork under `docs/supplemental-ui/product-logo.png` / `product-logo-dark.png`. Replace them with real logos, same filenames, and rebuild.

## Why two files

The brand mark sits on whatever the current theme’s background is — see [UI Bundle](../reference-ui-bundle/)'s theme section. `product_logo_dark` is swapped in automatically under the dark theme; omit it and `product_logo` is reused unchanged for both, which only reads well if the artwork already works on both backgrounds (a monochrome or already-inverted mark, for instance).

## Sizing

The brand mark’s slot is a small, roughly-square product mark next to a **separately rendered** text title (the site’s `title` from `docs/src/antora.yml`) — not a wide wordmark. A logo that already contains the product name as text usually duplicates what’s already there next to it.

`nav-brand.hbs` renders both images at a fixed **40×40 CSS px** (`width="40" height="40"`), so export at **at least 80×80** (2x, for HiDPI screens) — the seeded placeholder ships as a 256×256 PNG, which is generous headroom rather than a requirement. A transparent-background PNG or an SVG both work; square canvas, no padding baked into the file itself (the 40×40 box already gives it breathing room).

## Removing it entirely

Delete both keys — the side menu falls back to a text-only brand block (the site title alone, no mark) rather than failing the build.

---

# Versioning modes

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-versioning-modes/

`docouture new --mode` offers two shapes, both real and releasable — decided once, at scaffold time (`docouture upgrade` never changes it).

## Standalone (Stable + Prerelease) — the default

`main` always builds as the **prerelease** version (`docs/src/antora.yml`: `version: prerelease`, `prerelease: true`, permanently). A release force-moves a single rolling `stable` tag to a fresh commit — no historical archive, appropriate when only "now" and "what’s next" matter.

```
content:
  sources:
    - url: ..
      start_path: docs/src
      branches: [main]
      tags: ['stable']
```

## Versioned (Full History)

`main` still builds as the prerelease version — `docs/src/antora.yml` is byte-identical to the standalone shape on `main` — but every release is instead its own immutable `vX.Y.Z` git tag, kept forever. Appropriate for a library/SDK whose consumers pin an old version.

```
content:
  sources:
    - url: ..
      start_path: docs/src
      branches: [main]
      tags: ['v*']
```

A versioned-mode site additionally gets `docs/.release-version` — a plain-text file holding the **next** release’s target version, read by `docouture-release.yml` instead of a workflow input.

## On a release tag, `docs/src/antora.yml` changes

Standalone’s `stable` tag says `version: stable`, `prerelease: false`. A versioned release tag says `version: '1.2.0'` (or whatever was released), `prerelease: false`. Neither mode ever rewrites `main’s own copy.

## Which one to pick

Standalone if there’s one thing to document and only "current" matters. Versioned if past releases need to keep resolving unchanged after a new one ships — an SDK, a CLI, anything consumers pin a version of. See [Releasing a documentation](../guides-releasing-a-documentation/) for how a release is actually cut in either mode.

---

# Versioning &amp; publishing

Source: /1.0.0/main/guides-versioning-publishing/

Taking a site from a local build to a published, versioned one: the mode chosen at scaffold time, cutting a release, and the workflows that actually publish it.

- [Versioning modes](../guides-versioning-modes/) — Standalone (Stable + Prerelease) vs. Versioned (Full History), decided once at scaffold time.
- [Releasing a documentation](../guides-releasing-a-documentation/) — cutting a release via `docouture-release.yml`, manually or on a labelled merge to `main`.
- [Publishing a documentation](../guides-publishing-a-documentation/) — the prerelease and release publish workflows that run `docouture publish gh-pages`.
